items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Dave Amram Amarand had a weekend down there with me, and I was in the rhythm section

ctx.x: But they were teaching me like I never studied. But we got through that beautifully, and Alfred Lyon was very enthused -- he started calling me on quite a few record dates, and I got some calls from Herbie Irving Mann and a whole lot of people, different ones, but they had to get permission from in order to use me, and they signed me up with some options. Oh, but that was part of that New York scene.

Things kind of slowed up, and I worked a couple of gigs down at the Fire Spot Fireside and Dave Amram Amarand had a weekend down there with me, and I was in the rhythm section, and it was just a little hamburger joint on the Bowery there; we were

trying to make a little club out of it, and the next weekend, Ray Bryant came in on piano, and the following weekend, Herbie Nichols -- I was able to play with him; he was a genius. Beautiful young man -- not too long before he died. And then Thelonious said, "Come on down," and we with Trane and Shadow went down there, and we played -- and that was the gig. I stayed with that gig, plus recordings, first record it, still at Riverside now, and one night we had a recording date with Gerry Mulligan and Monk, called…
